name: Congenital Coronary Artery Fistula

criteria.description: Demonstration of abnormal communication between a coronary artery and a cardiac chamber or vessel by imaging modalities (e.g., echocardiography, coronary angiography, CT angiography, or MRI)
Presence of continuous cardiac murmur or signs of volume overload
Exclusion of acquired causes of coronary fistula such as trauma or iatrogenic injury

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Imaging confirmation of abnormal coronary artery to cardiac chamber or vessel communication
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis primarily relies on imaging; clinical signs support but are not definitive.

pathognomonic.notes: Heard best at left sternal border
searchTerms: heart murmur present all the time

pathognomonic.symptomName: Abnormal coronary artery to cardiac chamber communication detected on imaging
searchTerms: abnormal connection between heart artery and chamber on scan
coronary artery fistula seen on imaging
unusual heart vessel to chamber link

occasional.symptomName: Heart failure symptoms (e.g., peripheral edema, orthopnea)
searchTerms: signs of heart failure like swollen legs
reduced blood flow to heart muscle

laboratory: Generally nonspecific; may show elevated BNP if heart failure present
imaging: Echocardiography showing abnormal flow or dilated coronary artery
CT angiography or cardiac MRI confirming anatomy and shunt
genetic: No specific genetic markers identified; usually sporadic congenital anomaly
other: Electrocardiogram may show signs of left ventricular volume overload or arrhythmias

distinguishingFeatures: History of trauma, cardiac surgery, or invasive cardiac procedures
Later onset compared to congenital form
Connection between aorta and pulmonary artery rather than coronary artery
Different murmur characteristics and imaging findings
Shunt between ventricles rather than coronary artery to chamber

redFlags: Sudden onset chest pain or myocardial infarction
Signs of congestive heart failure in young patient
references: Gowda RM, et al. Coronary artery fistulas: clinical and therapeutic considerations. Int J Cardiol. 2006.
Yamanaka O, Hobbs RE. Coronary artery anomalies in 126,595 patients undergoing coronary arteriography. Cathet Cardiovasc Diagn. 1990.
Qureshi SA. Coronary artery fistulas. Orphanet J Rare Dis. 2006.
